newsitem.title: DENMARK: SAS seeks closer alliance with partners.
newsitem.headline: SAS seeks closer alliance with partners.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) said on Friday it and its bilateral foreign partners sought to deepen their alliances but did not give further details.
SAS is reported to be among airlines intending to build a new global alliance to challenge the planned British Airways and American Airlines linkup. SAS refuses to confirm or deny the reports.

"Since the inception of bilateral agreements between SAS, Lufthansa, United Airlines, Thai Airways International and Air Canada it has been the openly declared ambition of the partners to find ways in which collaboration may be deepened," an SAS statement said.

"To advance this process the partners...have established working groups and their managements have held meetings. At these talks both bilateral and multilateral aspects of deepening and broadening co-operation were discussed," it added, but gave no further information.
Industry sources have said that SAS, owned by the governments of Denmark, Norway and Sweden and private investors, plans to expand its current network of alliances.
The sources named Brazil's Varig, Japan's All Nippon Airways, South African Airways (SAA), Air Canada and British Midland as likely new partners.
SAA on Thursday denied any such plans, pointing out that it already had a successful relationship with American Airlines . SAS already has a partnership with Air Canada.
The Scandinavian carrier is battling growing competition in its home market, much of it from companies associated with BA.
On Thursday SAS appeared to hint that a new alignment was in the air when it said that any expansion of its existing alliances would leave its present ownership structure unchanged.
